target.founder: Cameron McCord, Bryce Strauss, Jason Hoch

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in AI & Software. Range: $2.0B - $3.8B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Nominal is a Series B-2 stage AI & Software company founded by Cameron McCord, Bryce Strauss, and Jason Hoch, currently valued at $1.0B on $155M raised. The valuation assessment draws from a peer universe of 3 same-sector companies at similar valuation tiers, supplemented by reference to a broader comp set including 1 public company (Palantir) and 8 private peers across the AI & Software frontier-tech landscape.

The peer-median method applied to the 3-company cohort yields $3.2B, grounded in direct comparables: Black Forest Labs at $3.2B (Series B), Field AI at $2.0B (Series B), and Ayar Labs at $3.8B (Series E). This method is applicable given stage and sector alignment with the target. The range across these peers spans $2.0B to $3.8B, providing a distributional anchor.

The triangulated valuation range is $2.8B (low), $3.2B (median), and $3.7B (high). The spread reflects variance within the peer set rather than divergence across multiple methodologies; only one method was applicable given data constraints. Key uncertainties include limited sample size (n=3), stage heterogeneity (one Series E peer), and reliance on a single valuation approach. The current $1.0B valuation sits materially below peer-median, suggesting either a discount to market comparables or a distinction in execution risk or revenue traction not captured in the peer universe.
